title: Morning Chest Pressure
scenarioIntro: 64-year-old man with known stable angina wakes with central chest pressure. 12-lead shows no STEMI. Tests ASA and nitro decision-making with reassessment, and destination reasoning.

callInformation.type: Chest pain, 64 M, conscious and breathing
dispatchNotes: Chest pain, 64 M, conscious and breathing

patientDemographics.name: Dennis Holloway
patientDemographics.appearance: Sitting on the edge of the bed, pale, diaphoretic, anxious, hand on chest.

patientPresentation: Alert and oriented, speaking full sentences, pale and diaphoretic, pressure 7/10 central chest radiating to L arm.
incidentNarrative: Woke at 0640 with central chest pressure, not relieved by rest. Wife called 911. Did not use his own nitro spray.

opqrst.onset: At rest, woke from sleep at 0640
opqrst.provocation: Not changed by position or breathing

medications: ASA 81 mg daily (last dose last night)
ASA 81 mg daily (last dose last night)

physicalExam.chest: Clear to bases bilaterally, no accessory muscle use, chest wall not tender.

withIncorrectTreatment: First nitro with BP checked: Pain 5/10, BP 146/88.
Nitro given without asking about PDE5 inhibitors: Instructor asks what the patient takes for erectile dysfunction. He took sildenafil two days ago.

expectedTreatment: 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of patient contact and interpreted
ASA 160 mg chewed after contraindication check
Nitroglycerin with BP before each dose and PDE5 inhibitor question
Transport to closest appropriate ED (no STEMI criteria)
protocolNotes: ALS PCS Cardiac Ischemia Medical Directive (ASA, nitroglycerin)
learningObjectives: Recognize ischemic chest pain and apply the cardiac ischemia directive

acrKeyFindings.finding: pain radiates to the left arm
asked about PDE5 inhibitors (erectile dysfunction medication)
